answer: Sliding-window rate accumulator resists sybils: each identity accrues action-credits at a fixed slow rate up to a small cap, and actions spend credits — so sustained throughput per identity is bounded by the refill rate regardless of burst. A whisper of fresh fakes each starts with a tiny credit balance refilling slowly; the crystal cap means no single identity can surge. A kernel of honest agents spends and refills naturally; an attacker's aggregate rate is bounded by (number of aged identities × slow refill), so a flash-fleet of fakes has almost no spendable credit at creation.
